events.text:
Trump’s endorsements in foreign elections have a 6–1 record so far, with Viktor Orbán’s defeat in Hungary his only loss, ahead of his newly announced backing of Benjamin Netanyahu.
🇵🇱 Poland: Karol Nawrocki won the 2025 presidential election after Trump administration officials urged Poles to vote for him.
🇦🇷 Argentina: Javier Milei’s party won October 2025 midterms after Trump threatened to withhold aid if it lost and the U.S. finalized a $20 billion currency swap.
🇭🇳 Honduras: Nasry Asfura won after Trump warned the U.S. would not keep funding Honduras if he lost, and pardoned Asfura’s party colleague, former President Juan Orlando Hernández, days before the vote.
🇨🇱 Chile: José Antonio Kast won the presidency after Trump’s endorsement.
🇯🇵 Japan: Sanae Takaichi’s party won a two-thirds supermajority in February’s snap election, three days after Trump’s “Complete and Total Endorsement,” and Trump later claimed credit.
🇨🇴 Colombia: Abelardo de la Espriella won the June runoff after Trump backed him.
🇭🇺 Hungary: Viktor Orbán lost in April to Péter Magyar’s Tisza party, which won about 53% of the vote and a two-thirds majority, despite a campaign visit by Vice President JD Vance.
🇮🇱 Israel: Netanyahu, endorsed ahead of the October 27 election, is the next test.

events.text:
BREAKING: Trump has given his "Complete and Total Endorsement" to Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 election, warning that the U.S. would have to take on Iran itself if Israel chose another leader. 
In a message addressed to Israelis, Trump called Netanyahu a "Great Warrior Prime Minister" and said Iran had been systematically destroyed militarily and financially, adding that unless it changes course, "we will soon finish the job." 
He wrote that if Israel elects "anyone other than Bibi," America would have to do this work itself, which he said he is not inclined to do. 
The endorsement comes as Netanyahu's Likud trails in polls behind former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party.

events.text:
🇺🇦 ⚠️ 🇺🇸 #Musk Asked #Trump To Slow Down #Ukraine's Military Defenses, Telegraph Exclusive Reveals: 
Elon Musk approached Donald Trump with the idea of slowing down Starlink in Ukraine, The Telegraph can reveal.
The billionaire tech entrepreneur approached the US president with the proposal to introduce speed limits on the system, which hampered Ukraine’s drone defences, according to four sources familiar with the discussions
One of the sources said Mr Trump “agreed” with Mr Musk’s suggestion, paving the way for the Pentagon to execute the slowdown on Starshield.
Mr Musk had previously blamed Mr Trump for the chaos, claiming any changes would have been decided by the US military and ultimately the president.
At the time, Mr Trump was embroiled in a row with Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries.
US officials had warned Kyiv’s team of peace negotiators that the U.S. could shut off intelligence-sharing and other kinds of support if the long-range attacks were not halted. 
Earlier this week, one of Mr Zelensky’s advisers said Mr Musk’s SpaceX had restricted access to the Starshield system, used by Kyiv to intercept jet-powered drones and strike behind enemy lines.
Speaking on the fringes of an EU summit on Friday, the Ukrainian president called the slowdown a “very dangerous and unpleasant surprise”.
Mr Musk denied he was responsible for limiting Starlink access, blaming the White House. He claimed that “any limits on speed or usage” were “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS”, referring to Mr Trump.
However, after what was described as a “night of carnage” in Kyiv because of the blackout, a senior source said Mr Musk had been alarmed about the possibility of adverse consumer reaction in Europe.
The source said: “He tweeted out that he was innocent and that it was the US administration that did it. The reality is that they were both in it.”
A high-ranking European official and two well-placed Ukrainian sources confirmed this version of events.
Speaking on Friday evening, Mr Trump said he did not think ‌either ‌he ⁠nor Mr Musk had been responsible for Ukraine ⁠losing Starlink access.
On Friday, an anonymous US official, cited in a report by the AFP, insisted that Trump did not make the request for a reduction of Starshield’s services for Ukraine. “No request was ever made by the president,” the US official said, after a report by Reuters claimed the decision came from the White House. 
The Pentagon has not publicly explained the restrictions.
The speed cap imposed on Ukraine limited drones using the Starshield system to around 160kmph, making it virtually impossible to intercept Russia’s barrages of jet-powered drones and missiles, which travel double the speed.
On Friday, Mr Zelensky said signals were being restored.
It is not the first time Mr Musk has been accused of limiting the use of his Starlink platform to the detriment of Ukraine.
In 2023, he confirmed he had rebutted requests by Kyiv to use the system in drone attacks on Crimea, the peninsula illegally annexed by Russia, to avoid being complicit in a “major act of war”.
Mr Musk was lauded by Ukrainians earlier this year for his direct role in blocking illegal access to Starlink by Russian soldiers fighting in Ukraine.
Radek Sikorski, Poland’s foreign minister, warned the tech billionaire: “As your European customers, we are watching you.”
The EU is planning to have its Iris2, a Starlink replacement, operational by 2030. Mr Zelensky arrived in Brussels bruised and seeking more support from his European allies after his war of words with Mr Trump.
Diplomats said leaders had advised the Ukrainian president to tone down his criticism of his US counterpart amid fears Washington could further withdraw its support for Kyiv.
Mr Trump has been highly critical of Ukraine’s strikes on Russia’s oil refineries, blaming them for soaring energy prices before the midterm elections next month.
More: www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/10/16/musk-approached-trump-slow-down-starlink-help-ukraine/

events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸 Ok, so my autistic side absolutely loves this thing. It's very impressive from an engineering perspective. If you've played any space/rocket sim like Kerbal Space Program, then you know what these are. It's basically an RCS (Reaction Control System) strapped to a car. It uses highly compressed nitrogen vented through thrusters to generate thrust, allowing the car to jump across distances. It's not really flying so much as jumping, kinda like in Rocket League.
But the rational part of my brain understands that this is a gimmick. We don't know the specifics of the final production system, but apparently, it has a 6,900 PSI tank in place of the passenger seats. That's roughly 470 times atmospheric pressure at sea level. If this thing enters a collision at high speed, then nothing is surviving the catastrophic rupture. The pressure wave alone will mincemeat the driver and everything around it.
TLDR; It’s a bomb. A land based Cruise Missile. What a visionary Elon truly is 😁

The family of US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee is still profiting from paid tours that promise American citizens access to senior Israeli officials, according to a Zeteo report.
The travel business, now run by Mike Huckabee’s son, and previously marketed as “The Israel Experience with Governor Mike Huckabee,” has taken hundreds of Americans to Israel over the years. 
🔴 the price tag is $5,250 per person, covering flights from New York, five-star hotels and meals
🔴 itineraries promise exclusive access, such as meetings with senior Israeli officials and evening lectures featuring hardline pro-Israel figures
🔴 Palestinian communities and towns are entirely absent from the tours
[A previous NYT report](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75870) found that Huckabee’s chief of staff, David Milstein, had diluted or blocked embassy assessments critical of Israel to present PM Benjamin Netanyahu’s government more favorably to President Donald Trump.
Milstein was also reported to have subjected staff to loyalty tests, asking whether they were “pro-Israel” or “pro-Hamas” - an approach that reportedly left some officials afraid to speak openly.
